name: Hemdan
overview: Hemdan was a male Edomite, identified specifically as the son of Dishon. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, situating him within the Edomite lineage. There are no additional notes or detailed accounts of his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Hemdan means "desirable," reflecting a positive attribute though it was not given by God. He is also referred to as Hamran in 1 Chronicles 1:41, though no specific meaning is provided for this variant.
familyAndRelationships: Hemdan is explicitly recorded as the son of Dishon, establishing his place within the Edomite family line. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further family connections for Hemdan.
scriptureSignificance: Hemdan's significance lies in his role as a named ancestor within the Edomite genealogy, which is important for understanding the broader biblical context of Israel's neighbors and relatives. His mention preserves the historical record of Edomite descendants, contributing to the biblical narrative's detailed genealogical framework.
